# Thirza Abernethy

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v4 c15 P1](../source/v04-c15.md#nw-v04-c15-p0001)</sub>
- **Status:** Alive  <sub>[v4 c15 P1](../source/v04-c15.md#nw-v04-c15-p0001)</sub>
- **Origin:** Brierley
- **Role:** Homemaker and farmer  <sub>[v1 c1 P9](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0009), [v1 c6 P29](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0029)</sub>

## Appearance

Thirza is a tall, slender woman with sharp angles rather than curves. She has dark hair streaked with gray that she wears tied tightly at the back of her head in a firm bun secured by wire hairpins. Around her mouth lies a subtle expression that hints at a hidden sense of humor.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P13](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0013)_

## Personality

Thirza possesses a limited background and a strict, unyielding sense of morality. She is suspicious of frivolousness and overly bright sunlight, preferring serious contemplation and methodical discipline. Though she disapproves of unbridled emotion, weeping, and pretend games, she displays deep integrity, fairness, and unexpected defense of children under her care when she feels they have been treated unjustly.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P9](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0009), [v1 c1 P13](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0013), [v1 c8 P7](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0007), [v1 c8 P15](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0015), [v1 c9 P26](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0026), [v1 c9 P28](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0028)_

## Traits

- Strict and moral  <sub>[v1 c1 P13](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0013)</sub>
- Disapproves of imaginative pretense  <sub>[v1 c8 P15](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0015), [v1 c8 P19](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0019)</sub>
- Fair and protective  <sub>[v1 c9 P26](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0026), [v1 c9 P28](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0028)</sub>
- Extremely neat and orderly  <sub>[v1 c1 P8](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0008), [v1 c1 P9](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0009)</sub>

## Abilities

- Domestic housekeeping and baking  <sub>[v1 c1 P8](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0008), [v1 c1 P9](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0009)</sub>
- Dairy farming and milking cows  <sub>[v1 c6 P29](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0029), [v1 c6 P37](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0037)</sub>
- Knitting  <sub>[v1 c1 P9](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0009)</sub>

## Goals

- To raise Nell dutifully and train her to be useful and well-behaved  <sub>[v1 c8 P7](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0007), [v1 c6 P34](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0034)</sub>

## History

Thirza Abernethy resided at Grey Shutters with her brother Obed. Expecting an orphan boy from Nova Scotia, she was initially shocked when Obed returned with an orphan girl named Nell Harcourt. Although uncertain about raising a young girl, Thirza agreed to keep Nell after considering it her duty and taking pity on her circumstances. Despite initially struggling with Nell's emotional outbursts and vivid imagination, Thirza defended Nell against harsh criticism from neighbor Agatha Sowerby. Over the years, Thirza diligently trained Nell into a composed, dependable young woman. Later in life, she took her very first long journey away from home to visit Seven Gulls and spend Christmas with the newly married Nell and Hugh Carrow.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P16](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0016), [v1 c3 P0](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0000), [v1 c3 P1](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0001), [v1 c6 P31](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0031), [v1 c8 P5](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0005), [v1 c9 P26](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0026), [v1 c9 P28](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0028), [v1 c30 P42](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0042), [v4 c15 P1](../source/v04-c15.md#nw-v04-c15-p0001)_

## Background by volume

- Daughter of a bashful farmer who established Grey Shutters on the border of his cleared land
- Lived her entire life within sixty miles of home at Grey Shutters  <sub>[v4 c15 P1](../source/v04-c15.md#nw-v04-c15-p0001)</sub>

## Quotes

> Agatha, it was wrong of you to mock her appearance.  <sub>[v1 c9 P26](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0026)</sub>

> No; you can just address me as Thirza. Being called Miss Abernethy is something I am unaccustomed to, and it would cause me to feel nervous.  <sub>[v1 c8 P9](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0009)</sub>

> I refuse to hold with picturing things other than how they actually exist.  <sub>[v1 c8 P19](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0019)</sub>
